incumbent.name: Tony Skinner
incumbent.summary: Tony Skinner, a Republican, was elected sheriff in November 2018 and is finishing his second four-year term, which ends in December 2026; state law bars him from seeking a third consecutive term, and he is running for the Delaware County Council District 3 seat instead {sp_skinner_council} {sp_mccall_removed}.
record: November 2018: Skinner, then a sergeant in the sheriff's office, defeated Democratic incumbent Sheriff Ray Dudley with 52.7% of the vote; he said he would target large-scale drug dealers and traffickers and take politics out of hiring and promotion decisions {bsd_skinner_2018}.

February 2019: The county council voted 4–3 to fund a $45 million justice center in the former Wilson Middle School, including a 500-bed jail; Skinner said the existing jail held more than 340 inmates in a space built for 220 and that the project, while unpopular, was needed {ipr_justice_center}.

February 2021: The sheriff's office moved 235 inmates into the new facility; Skinner said the old building had been 'completely maxed out' and that the county had been housing inmates in other counties' jails {fox59_jail_move}.

July 2023: The department's financial officer told the county council the jail had 10 corrections-officer openings; the department had spent more than $100,000 on overtime to cover shortages in 2021 and advertised starting pay of $38,166 {ipr_jail_staffing_2023}.
December 2025: Skinner announced his campaign for county council, citing his experience with the county budgeting process {sp_skinner_council}.

race_context: This is an open seat: Sheriff Tony Skinner is term-limited and is running for county council {sp_skinner_council}.

The Delaware County Election Board removed Republican James McCall from the May 5 primary ballot on Feb. 24, 2026; County Clerk Rick Spanger said McCall had not voted in two prior Republican primaries in Indiana, as required to run in a GOP primary. That left Chief Deputy Jeff Stanley as the Republican nominee, while Deputy Dave Williams was unopposed for the Democratic nomination {sp_mccall_removed}.
Both nominees work in the current sheriff's office: Stanley as chief deputy and Williams as a deputy {sp_mccall_removed} {in_list}.
Recurring issues for the office include jail staffing and overtime costs at the jail that opened in 2021 {ipr_jail_staffing_2023} {fox59_jail_move}.
No 2026 general-election candidate forum or debate for this race was found in available coverage.

candidates.summary: David (Dave) Williams is a Delaware County sheriff's deputy and sergeant with nearly 30 years in county law enforcement, including 18 years working in schools; he was unopposed for the Democratic nomination {sp_mccall_removed} {bsd_williams}.
background: Deputy with the Delaware County Sheriff's Department {sp_mccall_removed}.
Has nearly 30 years of law-enforcement experience in Delaware County and holds the rank of sergeant; he said he worked in the schools for 18 years {bsd_williams}.
path_to_ballot: Unopposed for the Democratic nomination in the May 5, 2026 primary {sp_mccall_removed} {in_list}.

items: Said it is 'very important' that people know their local sheriff personally, and that he wants residents to see county police agencies as 'here to help you guys' {bsd_williams}.

plans: No detailed platform was found in available coverage.

gaps: No campaign website or published platform found; coverage limited to one student-media profile (March 2026).
Search snippets suggest a Dave Williams ran in the 2022 Democratic primary for Delaware County sheriff; not verified.
A different David Williams is a Republican candidate for Delaware County Council District 1 (per search snippets); take care not to conflate them.

candidates.summary: Jeff Stanley is chief deputy of the Delaware County Sheriff's Department, with more than 30 years in county law enforcement; he became the Republican nominee after his only primary opponent was removed from the ballot {sp_mccall_removed} {stanley_site}.
background: Chief deputy of the Delaware County Sheriff's Department under Sheriff Skinner {sp_skinner_council} {sp_mccall_removed}.

His campaign says he has served Delaware County for more than 30 years in patrol, criminal investigations, SWAT, the bomb squad, search and recovery, and executive leadership as chief deputy {stanley_site}.
path_to_ballot: Announced his candidacy by December 2025 {sp_skinner_council}. Became the Republican nominee after the county election board removed James McCall from the May 5, 2026 primary ballot {sp_mccall_removed}.

items: Supports 'proactive policing that targets violent criminals, repeat offenders' and says deputies need training, equipment and support; pledges to enforce the law 'without political influence' {stanley_site}.

Supports jail programs in education, job readiness, substance-abuse recovery, peer support and vocational training to reduce repeat offenses, saying rehabilitation 'should never replace accountability' {stanley_site}.

Says the office has generated 'millions of dollars in revenue' by housing federal inmates and through other programs; pledges to pursue grants, invest in technology for deputy efficiency and evaluate every expenditure {stanley_site}.
Says the sheriff's office should be present in schools and at community events, and pledges to expand community outreach {stanley_site}.

on_incumbent: Is the chief deputy in the current administration; his campaign site cites the office's financial results 'over the past several years' and says he will 'continue' its approach {stanley_site}.
plans: Campaign lists four priorities: law and order, community partnerships, rehabilitation to reduce crime, and fiscal responsibility and innovation {stanley_site}.
endorsements_finance: No endorsements were listed on his campaign site, and no campaign-finance totals were found {stanley_site}.
gaps: A third-party ballot guide says he has been chief deputy since 2019 and holds a Ball State criminal-justice degree; not verified from a primary source.
Federal inmate-housing revenue figures are the campaign's claim; no county audit or budget document confirming the amount was reviewed.
No news coverage of his specific plans for jail staffing or pay was found.
